doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Booker Little and the Manassas circle
title: Coleman Hawkins's tenor left in the car on Central Avenue
summary: Lloyd tells how Hawkins left his saxophone on the back seat in Los Angeles and no one touched it, as a measure of respect.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: So dig this: When I graduated from college - So Booker and I would stay close, he’d come out with Max, you know, once or twice a year or something. I want to interject something - bring me back to that, but this is very interesting because - Booker was staying in a hotel called the Adams Hotel over there on Adams and Western. Somewhere around in there. That area, I don’t know what it is called, St. Andrews Place or something over in there.
Yeah, up on the West Side, you’re talkin’ about?
Yeah.
Yeah.
Coleman Hawkins was out in California doing that Central Avenue time for some

time, and he was living in a rooming house over there, and he liked this scotch and stuff. Well he would come home at night in his Chrysler, whatever he was driving - he always like Chryslers - and summertime he’d have the windows down and his tenor on the back seat! And he’d go up and go to bed!
And the tenor was still in the car?
Of course! You know why? That wouldn’t happen now, but you know why that happened?
Cause it was Coleman Hawkins.

Thank you. And all the pimps and the dope dealers and everybody knew you don’t mess with that! That’s our mana. That’s our stuff. You understand? That needs to brought to day, all these little boys talking about rappin’ and talkin’ about stuff, that was Coleman Hawkins!
Whoo! That’s heavy.
That’s God. You understand?
Whoa!
Now stop for a minute and think about that.
Now that is profound.
We’ll come back to the Booker thing.
That’s Doctor Profundus right there.
Thank you!
Oh my goodness. Well can I go here?
Yeah, but don’t let me - I’ll tell you about Booker.
